$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `conversations`' canonical store, the
NINTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM. One
entry per guard: per scope predicate, per vocabulary check that stands where
no enum stands, per shape check that stands where a migration-only CHECK
stands, per decision about a column the driver renders in a form the domain
cannot hold, and per statement the port's contract says must be one
statement. Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements
it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were
seen to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A TENTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json, mutations-cost.json, mutations-channels.json,
mutations-governance.json and mutations-secrets.json rather than an extension
of any of them, for the reason the fourth was: ten tranches are ten separate
claims about ten separate port surfaces, and a reader checking one should not
have to read past the other nine. All are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP, in one sentence per reason.
A TURN'S MONEY HAS NO COLUMNS. `Turn.cost` carries an amount, a step count,
an unpriced count and a completeness flag, and `Turn.usage` five token
figures; the `Turn` ROW carries `costCents` and nothing else of either. Six
of the nine numbers are rolled up from the STEP rows on every read, so a
store that answered them from a column that does not exist would report a
turn's bill as complete when it is a floor — and no returned value on a store
with one caller shows it.
THE DRIVER RENDERS A RATE IN A FORM THE DOMAIN CANNOT HOLD. `Decimal(24, 12)`
below 1e-7 comes back from the ORM as `"3e-7"`, and `domain/step-rates.ts`
requires the canonical decimal STRING because twelve fractional digits do not
survive a float. Two entries cover the expansion and the scale padding, and
both were found by the first integration run rather than by reading.
AND FOUR OF THE GUARDS PROTECT A TENANT BOUNDARY NO DATABASE RULE HOLDS.
`Thread.id`, `Turn.id`, `PostmanExecution.id` and
`PostmanExecution.contextHandle` are unique INSTALLATION-WIDE, and the handle
is a capability, so a `where` that lost its `environmentId` answers another
tenant's row to whoever holds the identifier. `InMemoryConversations` takes
the scope parameter on every method and ignores it, so the conformance
differential is structurally unable to see any of the four.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. Each suite set below was run UNMUTATED, on the same machine
and in the same container image, and required to be green with a non-zero
executed case count before its mutation was applied; a run reporting zero
executed cases is recorded as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE INTEGRATION SUITES RUN ON A REAL POSTGRESQL, in a container, on the
machine that has a daemon. `conversations-rows.test.ts` is the only suite
here that runs without one, and it is the one that reaches the mapping
branches a container suite cannot: a container only ever reads rows THIS
binary wrote, so the unknown-enum and half-written-rate branches are
unreachable from it.
THE SUITES ARE SIX AND NOT FOUR, because `max-file-lines` bit at the 500-line
HARD error twice and both seams it pointed at were real. The constraints suite
split into the shapes a CONVERSATION admits and the shapes a BILL and an
OPERATOR'S AUDIT ROW admit; the rules suite split into what happens when rows
are DESTROYED and what a caller may not reach or change. The shared scenario
split the same way, into the conversation and the operator's execution, and
both halves still write into ONE observation map so the differential still
compares one object per store.
EVERY `from` IS A UNIQUE SUBSTRING OF ITS FILE and is applied literally, so a
sweep that silently matched nothing is impossible: an entry whose `from`
occurs zero times or more than once is refused rather than swept.
THE FIRST SWEEP FOUND SEVEN SURVIVORS AND THEY ARE WHY SEVEN CASES EXIST.
M-C21 survived because every step fixture used sequence 1. M-C24 and M-C25
survived because one case sent a step carrying NEITHER a card nor its rates,
so whichever guard ran first refused it and deleting either changed nothing —
they are now two cases, each leaving the other half satisfied. M-C33 survived
because the frozen-column case asserts the write SUCCEEDS, so a lost scope
predicate was invisible to it. M-C34 survived because every earlier
measurement was taken on a ROOT thread, where the maximum and the minimum
depth are both zero. M-C39 survived because the earlier case asked for two
turns the planner happened to return in the requested order. M-C51 survived
because every earlier case ran inside ONE organization. Each is now a named
case rather than a widened entry.
RESULT, 2026-09-06, against PostgreSQL 16 (pgvector/pgvector:pg16) in a
container: 56 entries, 56 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS. Every baseline suite
set was green with a non-zero executed case count before its mutation was
applied, and every `from` matched its file exactly once.

mutations.name: M-C01 rows: Thread.status is validated, not cast
mutations.note: `WorkStatus` is one PostgreSQL enum shared by four tables. A binary older than a migration that ADDED a member reads a value it has never heard of, and a cast puts it into a transition table that has no row for it.
kills: every stored enum is validated rather than cast > a WorkStatus this binary has never heard of is refused, per table

mutations.name: M-C02 rows: Thread.compactionState is validated
mutations.from:
if (!(THREAD_COMPACTION_STATES as readonly string[]).includes(value)) {
    unreadable(UNKNOWN_COMPACTION_STATE, "Thread.compactionState", value);
mutations.note: Its own code rather than the WorkStatus one, because a compaction state and a work status are different columns with different remedies.
kills: every stored enum is validated rather than cast > an unknown compaction state and an unknown version bucket have separate codes

mutations.name: M-C03 rows: Turn.versionBucket is validated
mutations.from:
if (!(VERSION_BUCKETS as readonly string[]).includes(value)) {
    unreadable(UNKNOWN_VERSION_BUCKET, "Turn.versionBucket", value);
mutations.note: The bucket is the axis every canary judgement is drawn along; a third member read as a cast would put a turn in neither arm of the comparison.
kills: every stored enum is validated rather than cast > an unknown compaction state and an unknown version bucket have separate codes

mutations.name: M-C04 rows: Step rate sources are validated
mutations.from:
if (!(RATE_SOURCES as readonly string[]).includes(value)) {
    unreadable(UNKNOWN_RATE_SOURCE, column, value);
mutations.note: `ratesFullyObserved` decides a turn's `complete` flag by comparing the source to `UNAVAILABLE`; a value outside the union is neither, so a bill silently claims a confidence it does not have.
kills: a rate is read from three columns or from none > a rate source this binary does not know is refused, naming the column

mutations.name: M-C05 rows: a JSON column must be an object at its root
mutations.from:
if (typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
    unreadable(UNREADABLE_JSON_ROOT, column, Array.isArray(value) ? "a JSON array" : typeof value);
mutations.to:
if (false) {
    unreadable(UNREADABLE_JSON_ROOT, column, Array.isArray(value) ? "a JSON array" : typeof value);
mutations.note: The `*_json_root` CHECKs protect rows written while they were installed; a row predating one reaches the mapper, and a cast puts an array into a `Record` every reader then indexes.
kills: a JSON column is an object root or it is refused > an array in `Thread.sessionContext` is refused rather than indexed
a JSON column is an object root or it is refused > `Turn.input` and `Turn.output` are refused separately

mutations.name: M-C06 rows: an exponential decimal is expanded rather than refused
mutations.note: FOUND BY THE FIRST INTEGRATION RUN. The ORM renders `Decimal(24, 12)` below 1e-7 in exponential form, so an ordinary `cacheReadRate` of 0.000000300000 reads back as `"3e-7"` and every priced step becomes unreadable.
kills: a rate is read from three columns or from none > an EXPONENTIAL rate from the driver is expanded, not refused
a Decimal is read as a string or refused > an exponential COST is expanded to the cent scale too
the fake and the real store answer the same scenario identically

mutations.name: M-C07 rows: a decimal is padded to its COLUMN'S scale
mutations.note: `Decimal(24, 12)` stores twelve fractional digits. Without the padding a rate written as 0.000000300000 comes back as 0.0000003 — numerically right, and a difference that is not one to every caller comparing two rate books, including the conformance differential.
kills: a rate is read from three columns or from none > all three present is a rate, with the exact decimal STRING
a rate is read from three columns or from none > the scale is PART OF THE TYPE, so trailing zeros round-trip exactly
the fake and the real store answer the same scenario identically

mutations.name: M-C08 rows: a value finer than the scale is refused, not rounded
mutations.note: The column could not have held it, so reporting it would be reporting a number the database never stored — and the alternative to refusing is silently truncating a cost.
kills: a Decimal is read as a string or refused > a cost finer than Decimal(18, 6) is refused rather than rounded

mutations.name: M-C09 rows: a half-written rate has its own refusal
mutations.note: All twelve rate columns are nullable and `Step_usage_check` ties them together only when `costCents` is present, so a rate with no observation instant is a legal row and no `StepRate` can hold it.
kills: a rate is read from three columns or from none > present in SOME of the three is refused, with its own code

mutations.name: M-C10 rows: a NULL token column is a count of NONE
mutations.note: The domain makes the five counts non-nullable numbers and the schema makes them nullable integers; the reconciliation is that an absent count is a count of none, which is what `Step_usage_check` already assumes.

a turn's money comes from its steps and from nowhere else > usage is summed over the steps, cache figures kept apart

mutations.note: Six of the seven numbers in `TurnCost` have no column. A store that answered them from nowhere reports every turn as costing zero and being complete, which is a bill that overstates its own confidence in the one direction that matters.

mutations.note: `domain/step-usage.ts` records the measured defect this prevents: the extraction source reports 14,788 and 39,795 tokens for one turn from two places, because one counts the sub-agent steps and the other does not.

mutations.name: M-C13 guards: an identifier bound for @db.Uuid is checked first
mutations.note: A non-uuid is not a constraint failure at all: it is a driver conversion error partway through a transaction, with no SQLSTATE a caller can act on. The context's own `threadFixture` mints `thread-1` and its `stepFixture` a `modelPriceId` of `price-1`.
kills: @db.Uuid — a non-uuid identifier is a driver fault, not a constraint > the store refuses `thread-1`, which every in-memory double accepts
@db.Uuid on a step's price card > the store refuses `price-1`, which the context's own stepFixture mints

mutations.note: The rule's own clause is `cardinality = 0 AND forkedUpToTurnId IS NULL OR parent.id IS NOT NULL AND ...`; the two halves must be empty together.

mutations.name: M-C17 guards: the boundary is the LAST inherited turn
mutations.note: `NEW."forkedUpToTurnId" = NEW."forkedTurnIds"[cardinality(NEW."forkedTurnIds")]` is a rule stated nowhere but the migration, and a fork whose boundary is not its last ancestor replays a transcript that ends in the middle.
kills: Thread_ancestry — the fork lineage rule nothing outside the migration states > the store refuses a boundary that is not the LAST inherited turn

mutations.note: `Turn_usage_check` and `Step_usage_check` both refuse a negative latency and a negative cost, and both abort the caller's transaction when they do.

mutations.name: M-C20 guards: a row may not complete before it started
